A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Metalic research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved into the appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original ProteinGym experiments, trained baseline comparisons, component ablations, Reptile comparisons and attention analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and reports revised results for the longer-budget Reptile comparison.

M1.justification: The PLM and axial-attention architecture, preference objective, in-context meta-training and support-set-resampling fine-tuning procedure are retained. The revised fitness-embedding explanation in Section 3.2 and detailed Figure 6 document the architecture without establishing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ProteinGym single- and multi-mutant fitness prediction in zero-, 16- and 128-shot settings. No dataset, task family or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained across the benchmark experiments and appendices. Table 6 still compares Metalic with Reptile-3-3, Reptile-3-100 and Metalic-Reptile; their training budgets and scores change, not their identities.

E3.justification: Section 4.6 and Table 6 increase the reported comparison budget from 15,000 to 50,000 meta-training steps, and the compute-matched Metalic control from 45,000 to 150,000 steps. This is a localized protocol revision; the shot setting, metric, comparator configurations and gradient-computation matching remain the same.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 updates the controlled assessment of adding Reptile updates to Metalic, providing longer-budget evidence about whether accounting for fine-tuning during meta-training helps. The component ablations, training-data-size analysis, warm-up experiment and attention maps otherwise retain their evidence. NoAug merely moves from Table 5 to Appendix A.3, Table 9.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three training seeds, and retain the one-seed Reptile hyperparameter-tuning experiment. Updated standard deviations in Table 6 do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice or additional disclosed repetitions.

E6.justification: Table 6 replaces results under larger training budgets. At matched gradient-computation budgets, v1 reports Metalic at .553 ± .003 and Metalic-Reptile at .532 ± .006; v2 reports both at .562 ± .004. Reptile-3-100 changes from .528 ± .004 to .539 ± .001. These are changed-budget results, not same-setting gains. Other benchmark, ablation and appendix scores are retained.

T1.justification: The task definitions, objectives in Equations 1–4, Reptile update in Equation 5 and computational-complexity arguments are unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: efficient in-context meta-learning followed by fine-tuning, strong low-data ProteinGym performance, and competitive few-shot prediction with fewer parameters. The revised Reptile evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 shifts from suggesting that combining Reptile with Metalic may not justify its computational cost to emphasizing implementation complexity without a clear advantage. It now acknowledges comparable performance at equal computation rather than Metalic's earlier superiority. Existing multi-mutant-data limitations and attention-based interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link on the first page. Appendix A.2 newly states that hyperparameters are selected using single-mutant results and reused for multi-mutants. Appendix A.6 and Figure 6 disclose more architectural detail, including normalization, residual connections and embedding processing; these are documentation additions.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Coda-Forno et al. (2023), discussing meta-in-context learning with pretrained language models and its context-capacity and generalization limitations. This is a limited positioning addition. Changes to the Beck references otherwise concern bibliographic metadata and ordering.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the introduction, streamlines the meta-learning background and clarifies the architecture description. It moves the augmentation discussion into a dedicated appendix subsection and adds an architecture subsection, while retaining the overall narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds the detailed architecture diagram in Figure 6, separates the existing NoAug rows into appendix Table 9, and reorders Table 6. Appendix tables are regrouped and conference headers are added. The existing benchmark plots and attention-map images are retained.

improvement.justification: The longer-budget Reptile comparison tests the methodological conclusion at the standard training budget, and v2 appropriately revises the equal-compute interpretation from superiority to parity. Figure 6, the hyperparameter-selection explanation and the code link improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. These are useful but limited gains; the main method, benchmark coverage and headline results remain unchanged.
